title: Surface Assessment (P33)
description: An assessment reports, for each of the nine axes, what the repository does and what evidence supports the claim. It carries NO composite score, grade, level or ranking (program ruling R4). The four conditional requirements below are the schema half of P33 task 1.2 — the Go half is internal/assessment, where every field is unexported and the only way in is a constructor. Both halves exist because they guard different entrances: the type guards Go callers, the schema guards a stored row and a posted payload. internal/assessment/schema_test.go asserts every `enum` here equals its Go closed set exactly — in BOTH directions — so this file cannot become a second, drifting copy of a vocabulary.

source_revision.description: Half of the pin key. An assessment is OF a revision, which is why no finding here can be `stale` with respect to it.

agent_config_hash.description: The other half (FR16). Without it a finding cannot be attributed to the configuration that produced it.

findings.description: Exactly nine — one per axis, never fewer. An axis with nothing to say reports `not_measured` with its missing input; it is never dropped (FR1). `minItems`/`maxItems` bound the count; the set equality against the nine axes is checked in Go, where a duplicate can be named.

Finding.description: One axis's result. The nine keys three consumers switch on, plus the payload of exactly one state.

claim.description: The sentence a reader reads. Required in every state — a `not_measured` finding's claim IS "here is what is missing and what you could do", which is the difference between a report someone acts on and one they discount.

refusal_cause.description: Which of exactly three things this build lacks. Never a generic "unsupported": the three send a reader to three different places, and only one of them is the customer's problem.

allOf.$comment: state = not_measured ⇒ missing_input, and no other state may carry one. The negative half is as load-bearing as the positive one: a `refused` finding carrying a missing input renders in two different message shapes depending on which field a console checks first.
state = refused ⇒ refusal_cause, and no other state may carry one.

origin = inferred ⇒ BOTH attribution fields. Checked as a pair: a pin address with no model version records where an answer came from but not what produced it, so a provider's upgrade would still be invisible (design D7).

state = measured ⇒ an eval-set report, and no other state may carry one. Decisiveness travels with the score wherever the score is reported; a score that COULD arrive without it would eventually arrive without it.

The two illegal cells of the four-states × two-origins matrix. A measurement comes from an eval run, never from a model reading code; a refusal is a fact about THIS BUILD's capability, not a conclusion a model can reach.

EvidenceRef.description: A reference INTO an existing surface (design D5). The assessment is an index over evidence the platform already holds, never a second place a number is computed. No URL is stored: the surface owns its own route shape, and a stored URL is a copy of the router that eventually serves a 404.

fragment.description: Narrows to one part of the surface. Its ABSENCE means "the whole surface", never "unknown".

EvalSetReport.description: The properties that say HOW TO READ a score, on the same object as the score so they cannot be separated from it.

n_indecisive.description: Cases carrying an oracle that can never fail — the most misleading cases in a set, because they look measured and decide nothing.

coverage_measured.description: Whether oracle coverage was measured AT ALL. A separate boolean rather than a sentinel in `oracle_coverage`, because 0.0 is a number somebody measured and "we do not have this" is a different fact.

vacuous_dimensions.description: Coverage axes no case exercises. Named, not counted: "nothing to measure" is not "everything covered".

cases.description: The enumeration (FR13). A count is not a case list.

Interval.description: A measured value with its confidence interval and the number of seeds behind it. `n_seeds` is required and at least 1: no number is reported without the size of the set behind it (§7.1).

OracleVerdict.description: Whether this case's oracle can ever return "no", and when it cannot, why. Read from evalharness.Case.DecisiveOracle rather than recomputed — a second implementation of that probe would be a second answer to a question with one correct one.

allOf.$comment: An oracle that cannot fail must say why. "3 cases cannot fail" is a number; the reason is what turns it into a task.
